Challenges

What is keeping your e-commerce success at bay?

“I launched my online store, but no one seems to visit.”

New stores start invisible: no authority, thin categories, unindexed products. We build the crawlable structure and category content that give Google something to rank.

“My products aren’t showing up on Google.”

Usually indexation, duplicate variants or weak product content. We find which products are invisible and why, then fix it at template level.

“Competitors dominate search results in my category.”

They win on category depth, links and reviews. We map their advantage precisely and take the categories back in order of revenue.

“My site is slow, and customers leave before exploring.”

Heavy images and bloated themes tax every page. Speed work on templates lifts rankings and conversion together.

“Customers can’t find my store in their region.”

Regional demand needs regional pages and local signals. We build them with real substance, not copied city templates.

“I keep adding products, but organic visibility drops as the catalogue grows.”

Growth without crawl management dilutes the whole store. We set the rules — what gets indexed, what gets linked, what gets retired.

“I have hundreds of products, but Google isn’t discovering the important ones.”

Discovery runs through internal linking and sitemaps. We route both toward the products that carry your margin.

Our Process

The process behind winning e-commerce SEO

1

Complete store audit

Catalogue, crawl, indexation, speed and feed health — the full machinery inspected first.

2

Keyword & competitor analysis

Demand mapped by category and product, benchmarked against the stores outranking you.

3

Technical SEO for stores

Crawl budget, faceted navigation, canonicals and speed fixed at template level.

4

Product & category optimisation

The pages that sell, optimised for intent, content depth and conversion.

5

Catalogue & content optimisation

Buying guides and collection content that capture research-stage demand.

6

Structured data, feeds & AI shopping

Product, review and offer schema plus feed health — eligibility for rich results and AI shopping answers.

7

Link building for stores

Editorial links and digital PR aimed at category pages, not just the homepage.

8

CRO, tracking & continuous optimisation

Revenue tracked by category and product; the next fixes queued from the data.

FAQs

FAQs on e-commerce SEO services

Which platforms do you work with?

Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, Webflow and custom builds — the strategy adapts to each platform’s constraints.

Should we optimise every product page?

No. We prioritise by revenue and search demand; long-tail products are handled with templates and rules.

How do you handle seasonal products?

With a calendar that builds authority before peak season and preserves it after, instead of starting from zero each year.

Can SEO work alongside our PPC?

Yes — shared keyword data makes both cheaper: PPC tests fast, SEO compounds on what converts.

How long before e-commerce SEO affects revenue?

Technical and template fixes can lift crawl and index coverage within weeks; category rankings and the revenue that follows typically build over 3–6 months, faster in less competitive niches.

Do you also optimise our product feed?

Feed health is part of setup and monitoring — clean titles, attributes and availability keep your products eligible for free listings and shopping surfaces, which support the organic program.

What happens to out-of-stock products?

They are a quiet authority leak. We apply a deliberate strategy per case — keep and optimise evergreen pages, redirect true dead-ends to the closest live category, and never let filters multiply them into junk URLs.

How is success reported?

On revenue, not just rankings: organic sessions, add-to-carts and sales by category and product, tracked in SERPLoft™ alongside the rankings that drive them.
